-49.25539,-16.69788.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

-68.24700,44.35600.name: The Jackson Laboratory
-68.24700,44.35600.desc: A non-profit that is also the world’s largest supplier of genetically defined mice, holding more than eleven thousand strains and shipping millions of animals a year. Its catalogue is the reason a paper published in one country can be repeated in another: the strain has a number and anyone with an institutional account can order it. That same catalogue is a list of thousands of lineages bred to be ill in a particular way, maintained in perpetuity because a researcher somewhere may want them. Mice are excluded from the US Animal Welfare Act’s definition of an animal, so almost none of this appears in any official count.

-74.07600,4.59810.name: Corte Constitucional de Colombia — Sentencia T-968 de 2009
-74.07600,4.59810.desc: The 2009 judgment that is the entire legal basis for surrogacy in Colombia. It held that nothing in Colombian law expressly prohibits such agreements, and set out conditions for them — but it did not create a framework for the contract, for parentage, or for the medical and financial obligations owed to the surrogate. One summary puts it exactly: the court authorised surrogacy without regulating it. More than sixteen bills to legislate have been introduced over roughly two decades and none has passed, so the practice runs on judicial tolerance, with the court issuing further rulings since. In practice the surrogate may appear on the birth certificate and parentage is established after birth through court proceedings, which vary by judge. This is the third distinct legal condition this facet now records: a country that regulates surrogacy, a country that prohibits it, and a country where it exists because nothing forbids it.
